record.title: Keszegh–Lemons–Martin–Pálvölgyi–Patkós extension conjecture for induced saturation
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset on $[p]$, and let $\dot P$ be the poset on $[p+1]$ obtained by adjoining a new element that dominates every element of $P$. Let $\text{sat}^*(n,P)$ denote the minimum size of an induced $P$-saturated family of subsets of $[n]$. **Keszegh–Lemons–Martin–Pálvölgyi–Patkós's extension conjecture.**

$$
\text{sat}^*(n,P)=O(1)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad\text{sat}^*(n,\dot P)=O(1).
$$

This conjecture concerns which posets have bounded induced saturation number and is presented as an open research direction in the paper. No resolution is given.
record.source_name: Andrea Freschi, Simón Piga, Maryam Sharifzadeh and Andrew Treglown, “The induced saturation problem for posets”, arXiv:2207.03974 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03974

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2022). “Curiously, it remains open as to whether our result is essentially best possible or not.”

record.title: Ning–Lu–Wang spectral-radius conjecture for edge connectivity
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}_{n}^{\kappa',\delta}$ be the set of graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $\kappa'$. Let $B_{n,\delta+1}^{\kappa'}$ be the graph obtained from $K_{\delta+1}\cup K_{n-\delta-1}$ by adding $\kappa'$ edges joining one vertex in $K_{\delta+1}$ to $\kappa'$ vertices in $K_{n-\delta-1}$. **Ning–Lu–Wang conjecture.** For $4\leq\kappa'<\delta$, $B_{n,\delta+1}^{\kappa'}$ is the graph with the maximum spectral radius in $\mathcal{A}_{n}^{\kappa',\delta}$. The source says that this conjecture is settled by the paper's results, but the supplied excerpt does not state the exact resolving theorem or its hypotheses.
record.source_name: Dandan Fan, Xiaofeng Gu and Huiqiu Lin, “Spectral radius and edge-disjoint spanning trees”, arXiv:2207.04701 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.04701

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Existence of class-0 non-affine knots with genus different from 1
record.statement: In $\mathbb{R}P^3$, a knot is called **class-$0$** if it has class $0$, and a knot is **non-affine** if it is not affine. Its genus is the minimum genus of a good surface bounding it. **Existence conjecture.** There exist class-$0$ non-affine knots whose genus is not equal to $1$. The preceding discussion constructs infinitely many class-$0$ non-affine knots of genus $1$; this conjecture asks whether such knots also occur with a different genus.
record.source_name: Rama Mishra and Visakh Narayanan, “Geometry of knots in real projective 3-space”, arXiv:2207.05392 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05392

record.title: Hamilton-cycle time-and-budget trade-off conjecture
record.statement:
Let a **$(t,b)$-strategy** $B$ of Builder be a strategy that observes at most $t$ arriving edges and purchases at most $b$ of them. A graph is **Hamiltonian** if it contains a Hamilton cycle. **Hamilton-cycle time-and-budget trade-off conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, if

$$
t\le(1+\varepsilon)n\log n/2\quad\text{and}\quad b\le(1+\varepsilon)n,
$$

then for any $(t,b)$-strategy $B$ of Builder,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} \mathbb{P}(B_t\text{ is Hamiltonian})=0.
$$

The conjecture says that simultaneously near-optimal observation time and near-optimal budget do not suffice to construct a Hamilton cycle with high probability. It complements the paper's results showing success when either time or budget is inflated by a constant factor.
record.source_name: Alan Frieze, Michael Krivelevich and Peleg Michaeli, “Fast construction on a restricted budget”, arXiv:2207.07251 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Continuity conjecture for the Rényi entropy rate at order one
record.statement:
Let $Z=\{Z_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a stationary ergodic process over a finite alphabet $\mathcal{Z}$. Its Shannon entropy rate is

$$
H(Z)\triangleq \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{H(Z_1^n)}{n},
$$

and, when the limit exists, its $\alpha$-th order Rényi entropy rate is

$$
H_{\alpha}(Z)\triangleq \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{H_{\alpha}(Z_1^n)}{n}.
$$

**Continuity conjecture.** For every stationary ergodic process $Z$,

$$
\lim_{\alpha\rightarrow 1}H_{\alpha}(Z)=H(Z).
$$

The conjecture is a natural rate-level analogue of the finite-block identity $\lim_{\alpha\rightarrow 1}H_{\alpha}(Z_1^n)=H(Z_1^n)$, but the existence of the Rényi entropy rate itself is not known for general stationary ergodic processes. The source reports this conjecture as neither proved nor disproved in the literature.
record.source_name: Chengyu Wu, Yonglong Li, Li Xu and Guangyue Han, “Renyi Entropy Rate of Stationary Ergodic Processes”, arXiv:2207.07554 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07554

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2022). “However, this conjecture is neither proved nor disproved in the literature.”

record.title: Logarithmic-component conjecture for irreducible foliation components
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma\subset\textsf{Fol}_d(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C})$ be an irreducible component, and let $\delta_2(\Sigma)$ denote the corresponding minimum second subdistribution degree. Let $\textsf{Log}_{(d_1,d_2)}(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C})$ be the logarithmic component associated with positive integers $d_1$ and $d_2$.

**Logarithmic-component conjecture.** If $\delta_2(\Sigma)=d$, then there exist integers $d_1$ and $d_2$ such that

$$
\Sigma=\textsf{Log}_{(d_1,d_2)}(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}).
$$

This is the component-level form of the preceding claim, asserting that every irreducible component with the extremal invariant is logarithmic. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Wodson Mendson and Jorge Vitório Pereira, “Codimension one foliations in positive characteristic”, arXiv:2207.08957 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.08957

record.title: Bessel-number formula for generalized Eulerian triangles
record.statement:
Let $p\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\zeta\in\{0,1\}$, and let $c$ be arbitrary. Write $E_{n,k}(-1,2;c_0,c_\infty)$ for the generalized Eulerian triangle, and let $B_{\nu,\kappa}=S_{\nu,\kappa}(1,2;0)$ and $B^{(r)}_{\nu,\kappa}=S_{\nu,\kappa}(1,2;r)$ denote the Bessel and $r$-Bessel numbers. For $a\in\mathbb{C}$, write $a^{\overline m,2}=a(a+2)\cdots(a+2(m-1))$ for the step-$2$ rising factorial, with $a^{\overline{0},2}=1$. **Bessel-number formula.** For all admissible $n,k$, one has

$$
E_{n,k}(-1,2;c+2p+\zeta,2p+\zeta)=\frac{(c+2p+\zeta)^{\overline n}}{(c+2p+2\zeta)^{\overline p,2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^p\frac{(c+1)^{\overline p,2}}{(c+1)^{\overline{k+\ell},2}}B_{2p+\zeta,2p+\zeta-\ell}B^{(2p+\zeta-2\ell)}_{n,n-k}.
$$

The identity was suggested by experimentation with repeated contiguous transformations of generalized Eulerian triangles. A proof and a combinatorial interpretation were stated to be lacking, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Robert S. Maier, “Triangular Recurrences, Generalized Eulerian Numbers, and Related Number Triangles”, arXiv:2207.10224 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.10224

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Keevash–Sudakov conjecture on monochromatic copies and Turán numbers
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, and let $f(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges not contained in any monochromatic copy of $H$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_n$. **Keevash–Sudakov conjecture.** For any graph $H$ and sufficiently large $n$, 

$$
f(n,H)=ex(n,H).
$$

The paper notes that its main theorem provides counterexamples with chromatic number $3$, so the conjecture is false in general.
record.source_name: Xiutao Zhu and Yaojun Chen, “Turán number for odd-ballooning of trees”, arXiv:2207.11506 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1908.02025](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.02025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.11506

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Dimension-degree tower-height conjecture for semi-algebraic Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
Let $R_r^{d,D,m}(n)$ be the Ramsey number for $r$-uniform semi-algebraic hypergraphs with dimension $d$, degree bound $D$, and $m$ defining polynomials. Let $s=\min\{d,D\}$. Write $\operatorname{tw}_j(x)$ for the tower function of height $j$ with an $x$ at the top.

**Dimension-degree tower-height conjecture.** There exists a function $k:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that, for integers $r,d,D,m$, there is a constant $c=c(r,d,D,m)$ satisfying

$$
R_r^{d,D,m}(n)<\operatorname{tw}_{k(s)}(n^c).
$$

The conjecture predicts that the tower height depends on the minimum of the ambient dimension and polynomial degree, rather than directly on the uniformity. The text presents this as an open challenge, especially in low-dimensional or low-degree cases.
record.source_name: Zhihan Jin and István Tomon, “Ramsey numbers of semi-algebraic and semi-linear hypergraphs”, arXiv:2208.01010 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.01010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Annular folded ribbonlength conjecture for unknots with prescribed linking number
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $\mathcal{U}_{w,F}$ be a folded ribbon unknot that is a topological annulus, with ribbon linking number ${\operatorname{Lk}}(\mathcal{U}_{w,F})=\pm n$. Let ${\operatorname{Rib}}$ denote folded ribbonlength. **Annular folded ribbonlength conjecture.** The minimum folded ribbonlength is

$$
{\operatorname{Rib}}([\mathcal{U}_{w,F}])=2n.
$$

The theorem preceding this conjecture proves the value $2n$ when the writhe is zero. The conjecture asserts that allowing nonzero writhe cannot produce a smaller folded ribbonlength; folds and crossings each contribute at least $2$ in the relevant lower-bound argument.
record.source_name: Elizabeth Denne and Troy Larsen, “Linking number and folded ribbon unknots”, arXiv:2208.03239 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03239

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “This open problem is not the focus of this paper.”

record.title: Equality of spectral-radius limits for generalized affine fractal interpolation functions
record.statement:
Let $I=[0,1]$ be the domain, let $S$ be the vertical scaling function, and let $M_k$ and $M'_k$ be the matrices associated with the $k$-th subdivision, with spectral radii denoted by $\rho(M_k)$ and $\rho(M'_k)$, respectively. Assume that the vertical scaling function $S$ is not identically zero on every subinterval of $I$. **Spectral-radius limit conjecture.** Then

$$
\lim_{k\to \infty}\rho(M_k)=\lim_{k\to \infty}\rho(M'_k).
$$

The equality would identify the limiting spectral radius obtained from the upper and lower matrix approximations, supporting the spectral-radius formula used to determine the box dimension of the generalized affine fractal interpolation function. The supplied text does not indicate whether this assertion has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Lai Jiang and Huo-Jun Ruan, “Box dimension of generalized affine fractal interpolation functions”, arXiv:2208.04126 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04126

record.title: The maximal Euler characteristic conjecture for multipath complexes
record.statement:
Let ${\tt K}_n$ be the complete digraph on $n$ vertices, with a bidirectional edge between every pair of vertices. Let ${\tt G}$ be any digraph on $n$ vertices, and write $X(-)$ for the multipath complex and $\widetilde{\chi}$ for reduced Euler characteristic.

**Maximal Euler characteristic conjecture.**

$$
\widetilde{\chi}(X({\tt K}_n))\geq \widetilde{\chi}(X({\tt G})).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the complete digraph has the largest reduced Euler characteristic among multipath complexes of digraphs on $n$ vertices. It was verified computationally for $n<8$ in the source, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Luigi Caputi, Carlo Collari, Sabino Di Trani and Jason P. Smith, “On the homotopy type of multipath complexes”, arXiv:2208.04656 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: The lower-bound conjecture for DET:IC density in cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $\textrm{DET:IC\%}(G)$ denote the minimum density of a deterministic error-detecting identifying code in $G$. **Lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
\textrm{DET:IC\%}(G) \ge \frac{3}{4}.
$$

The paper identifies $\frac{3}{4}$ as the lowest value found for cubic graphs and exhibits infinite families attaining this density. Whether every cubic graph satisfies the bound remains conjectural in the provided text.
record.source_name: Devin Jean and Suk Seo, “Optimal Error-detection system for Identifying Codes”, arXiv:2208.06052 (2022).

record.title: Kalai's affine-stress reconstruction conjecture up to affine type
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 4$, let $2\leq i\leq d/2$, and let $P$ be a simplicial $d$-polytope. A missing face is a vertex set whose proper subsets are faces but which is not itself a face.

**Kalai's affine-type reconstruction conjecture.** If $P$ has no missing $(d-1)$-faces, then its graph and the space of affine $2$-stresses determine $P$ up to affine equivalence. More generally, if $P$ has no missing faces of dimension at least $d-i+1$, then the space of affine $i$-stresses determines $P$ up to affine equivalence.

This strengthens reconstruction of combinatorial type by seeking the affine realization itself. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Isabella Novik and Hailun Zheng, “Affine stresses: the partition of unity and Kalai's reconstruction conjectures”, arXiv:2208.06693 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2106.09284](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09284).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06693

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Partial converse for monochromatic triangles in symmetric $v_{3}$ configurations
record.statement:
Let a **symmetric $v_{3}$ configuration** be a configuration whose lines are arranged so that each line contains three points and each point lies on three lines. Suppose such a configuration contains a maximal set of mutually intersecting lines of size $i$. A **line $2$-coloring** assigns one of two colors to each line, and a monochromatic triangle is a triangle whose three lines have the same color. **Partial converse conjecture.** If the minimum number of monochromatic triangles over all line $2$-colorings is non-zero, then

$$
i>4.
$$

This conjecture proposes a partial converse to the preceding theorem relating the size of mutually intersecting line sets to the minimum number of monochromatic triangles. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Jamie Bishop, Rebekah Kuss and Benjamin Peet, “Variations on Ramsey numbers and minimum numbers of monochromatic triangles in line 2-colorings of configurations”, arXiv:2208.06912 (2024).

record.title: The two embedded geodesic lines conjecture for complete Riemannian planes
record.statement: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian plane, meaning a complete Riemannian surface homeomorphic to the plane. An **embedded geodesic line** is the image $c(\mathbb R)$ of an injective, proper geodesic $c\colon\mathbb R\to M$. **The two-line conjecture.** Every complete Riemannian plane has at least two embedded geodesic lines. The theorem stated immediately before this conjecture constructs a complete Riemannian plane with precisely two embedded geodesic lines, while earlier work establishes existence of at least one; thus the conjecture would determine the maximal universal lower bound.
record.source_name: Victor Bangert and Stefan Suhr, “A Riemannian plane with only two injective Geodesics”, arXiv:2208.08475 (2022).

record.title: Maximum degree of noninvertibility for promotion on posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be an $n$-element poset, and let $\partial$ denote promotion on labelings of $P$. Write $\deg(\partial)$ for its degree of noninvertibility.

**Maximum noninvertibility conjecture.** For any poset $P$,

$$
\deg(\partial)\leq\frac{(n+2)(n+1)}{6}.
$$

In other words, the degree of noninvertibility of promotion should be largest when $P$ is a chain. The stated value is attained for an $n$-element chain, while the general inequality remains open.
record.source_name: Eliot Hodges, “On Promotion and Quasi-tangled Labelings of Posets”, arXiv:2208.08665 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08665

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “Finally, in , we present several open problems and further directions of inquiry.”

record.title: The bow-tie exception conjecture for locally irregular decompositions
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{T'}$ be the family consisting of the recursively defined family $\mathfrak{T}$, all odd-length paths and all odd-length cycles, and let $B$ denote the bow-tie graph. For a graph $G$, let ${\rm lir}(G)$ be the least number of locally irregular graphs into which $G$ can be decomposed. **Bow-tie exception conjecture.** Every connected graph $G\notin\mathfrak{T'}$, except for the bow-tie graph $B$, satisfies

$$
{\rm lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$

The bow-tie graph is known not to admit a decomposition into three locally irregular graphs, while the conjecture has been proved for trees, cacti, sufficiently high minimum degree, and sufficiently large regular degree. It remains open for general connected graphs.
record.source_name: Igor Grzelec and Mariusz Woźniak, “On decomposing multigraphs into locally irregular submultigraphs”, arXiv:2208.08809 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08809

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “This conjecture remains still open, but there are some important results about the 1-2-3 Conjecture and we refer the reader to the survey .”

record.title: The linear arithmetic fundamental lemma for general Hecke functions
record.statement:
Let $E_0=F\times F$, let $E_1$ and $E_2$ be quadratic extensions of $F$, and let $E_3\subset E_1\otimes_F E_2$ be the third quadratic extension. Let $\alpha:(E_0,E_3)\to M_{2n}(F)$ be a regular semi-simple pair of embeddings matching a pair $\beta:(E_1,E_2)\to\operatorname{End}^0(\mathbb{X})$. For $f\in\mathcal{H}$, let $\operatorname{\partial Orb}(\alpha,f)=(2\log q_F)^{-1}\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right\vert_{s=0}O(\alpha,f,s)$, and let $\operatorname{Int}(\beta,f)$ be the associated intersection number.

**Linear arithmetic fundamental lemma.** For every $f\in\mathcal{H}$, there is an equality up to sign,

$$
\pm \operatorname{\partial Orb}(\alpha,f)=\operatorname{Int}(\beta,f).
$$

This conjecture extends the basic AFL identity from the characteristic function of the standard maximal compact subgroup to arbitrary spherical Hecke functions. The source says that it concerns precisely the invariants with $\operatorname{ord}(\delta)=1$, but provides no resolution status.
record.source_name: Qirui Li and Andreas Mihatsch, “On the Linear AFL: The Non-Basic Case”, arXiv:2208.10144 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10144

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Thomas–Williams' cyclic sieving conjecture for rational Tamari lattices
record.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be relatively prime positive integers, let $\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)$ be the rational Tamari lattice, and let $\operatorname{Row}$ be its rowmotion operator. Define the $q$-integer $[k]_q=(1-q^k)/(1-q)$ and the $q$-binomial coefficient ${{a+b\brack b}_q}$ in the usual way. Set

$$
\operatorname{Cat}^{(a,b)}(q)=\frac{1}{[a+b]_q}{a+b\brack b}_q.
$$

**Thomas–Williams' cyclic sieving conjecture.** The triple

$$
(\operatorname{Tam}(a,b),\operatorname{Row},\operatorname{Cat}^{(a,b)}(q))
$$

exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.

This conjecture strengthens the rowmotion-order conjecture by predicting the complete orbit structure through evaluations of the rational Catalan polynomial. It is proved in the paper for $m$-Tamari lattices, but remains open for arbitrary rational Tamari lattices.
record.source_name: Colin Defant and James Lin, “Rowmotion on m-Tamari and BiCambrian Lattices”, arXiv:2208.10464 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Star-like graph mode conjecture for domination polynomials
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $D(G,x)$ be its domination polynomial, and call the index of a largest coefficient its **mode**. A graph is **star-like** in the sense intended by the source. **Star-like graph mode conjecture.** For each order $n$, there is a star-like graph whose domination polynomial has its mode at the largest index among all graphs of order $n$ without isolated vertices.

The conjecture is motivated by the relationship between the mode of a domination polynomial and the average order of dominating sets, together with computational evidence. The supplied material gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Iain Beaton and Ben Cameron, “A Tight Upper Bound on the Average Order of Dominating Sets of a Graph”, arXiv:2208.10475 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10475

record.title: The minimum eccentricity-entropy conjecture for graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $I_{ecc}(G)$ denote its eccentricity-entropy. An extremal graph is one attaining the minimum value of this entropy. **The minimum eccentricity-entropy conjecture.** Among graphs of order $n$, the minimum value of $I_{ecc}$ is attained by the graph obtained by removing a small number of edges from the complete graph of order $n$. In particular, extremal graphs of order $n$ have $k\geq \frac{n}{2}$ vertices of degree $n-1$. The paper states that this conjecture is true except for the assertion concerning the removal of a small number of edges.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie and Yanni Dong, “On the main distance-based entropies: the eccentricity- and Wiener-entropy”, arXiv:2208.12209 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12209

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2022). “Finally, Conjecture () is disproved.”

record.title: Conjecture on the nonbipartite Ramsey number for $C_4$-free color classes
record.statement:
Let $r(K_n,C_4,3)$ denote the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_n$ with no monochromatic copy of $C_4$ in the relevant 3-color configuration.

**Nonbipartite Ramsey conjecture.**

$$
r(K_{n}, C_4, 3) = \frac{n}{2} + O(1)
$$

and

$$
r(K_{n}, C_4, 3) = \frac{n-1}{2}
$$

for infinitely many $n$.

The paper proves the weaker estimate $r(K_n,C_4,3)=n/2+O(n^{1-\delta})$ for some $\delta>0$. The conjecture asks whether the error term can be improved to $O(1)$ and whether the lower bound is attained infinitely often; this is related to essentially resolvable Steiner triple systems whose pairs of color classes have union of girth $5$.
record.source_name: Felix Joos and Dhruv Mubayi, “Ramsey theory constructions from hypergraph matchings”, arXiv:2208.12563 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Maximum-degree forcing conjecture for graphs with large spectral radius
record.statement:
Let $s\geq 1$ be an integer, and let $f(s)$ be a function of $s$. Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with $n\geq f(s)$, and let $\rho(G)$ denote its spectral radius. **Maximum-degree forcing conjecture.** If

$$
\rho(G)\geq \frac{1+\sqrt{4(n-s)+1}}{2},
$$

then $G$ contains either the star $K_{1,n-s}$ or a $4$-cycle $C_4$. This conjecture is proposed as a generalization of the preceding extremal results for $C_4$-free graphs; the source provides no resolution, and in particular leaves the function $f(s)$ unspecified.
record.source_name: Zhiwen Wang and Ji-Ming Guo, “Maximum degree and spectral radius of graphs in terms of size”, arXiv:2208.13139 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.13139

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2022). “The conjecture was confirmed by Zhai and Wang in .”

record.title: The quadratic distinct-angle conjecture in general position
record.statement:
For $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $A_{\mathrm{gen}}^{(d)}(n)$ denote the minimum number of distinct angles formed by a set of $n$ points in general position in $\mathbb R^d$, where general position means no three points are collinear and no four points lie on a circle. **Quadratic distinct-angle conjecture.** Both quantities satisfy

$$
A_{\mathrm{gen}}^{(2)}(n)=\Theta(n^2)\qquad\text{and}\qquad A_{\mathrm{gen}}^{(3)}(n)=\Theta(n^2).
$$
 The paper gives $O(n^2)$ constructions in both dimensions, so the conjecture asserts that these constructions are optimal up to constant factors.
record.source_name: Ruben Ascoli, Livia Betti, Jacob Lehmann Duke, Xuyan Liu, Wyatt Milgrim, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson, Francisco Romero Acosta and Santiago Velazquez Iannuzzelli, “Distinct Angles and Angle Chains in Three Dimensions”, arXiv:2208.13284 (2023).

record.title: Semistrong chromatic index bound beyond complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $K_{n,n}$ denote a complete bipartite graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{ss}}'(G)$ denote the maximum degree and semistrong chromatic index of $G$, respectively. **Semistrong index improvement conjecture.** If $G$ is distinct from $K_{n,n}$, then

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{ss}}'(G)\le \Delta(G)^2-1.
$$

The paper proposes this improvement because its general bound is tight for complete bipartite graphs, while no other connected extremal family is known; its resolution is not given.
record.source_name: Borut Lužar, Martina Mockovčiaková and Roman Soták, “Revisiting Semistrong Edge-Coloring of Graphs”, arXiv:2208.13297 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.13297

record.title: Subcubic semistrong chromatic index conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $3$, let $K_{3,3}$ be the complete bipartite graph, let the $5$-prism be the graph named in the source, and let $\chi_{\mathrm{ss}}'(G)$ denote the semistrong chromatic index of $G$. **Subcubic semistrong index conjecture.** If $G$ is distinct from $K_{3,3}$ and the $5$-prism, then

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{ss}}'(G)\le 7.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the claim that the $5$-prism is the only known connected subcubic graph with semistrong chromatic index $8$, together with computational verification for small subcubic graphs; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Hartnell's characterization of bipartite graphs partitionable into two-colored domination sets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected bipartite graph. A **two-colored $\gamma$-set** of $G$ is a minimum dominating set $D\in \underline{MDS}(G)$ that can be partitioned as $D=D_1\cup D_2$ with

$$
V(G)-N_G[D_1]=D_2,\qquad V(G)-N_G[D_2]=D_1.
$$

**Hartnell's characterization.** If $V(G)$ can be partitioned into two-colored $\gamma$-sets, then $G$ is the $4$-cycle or $G$ can be obtained from $K_{2t,2t}$ by removing the edges of $t$ vertex-disjoint $4$-cycles.

This gives a proposed structural characterization of connected bipartite graphs whose vertex sets admit such a partition. The supplied source does not state whether the characterization has been proved or remains open.

record.title: Hafner's recursive leading-monomial conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
record.statement:
Fix $w\in S_n$ and any term order with $x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_n$. Let $\mathfrak{G}_w^{(k)}$ denote the degree-$k$ homogeneous component of $\mathfrak{G}_w$, and let $m_k(\bm{x})$ be its leading monomial. The Rajchgot index $\mathrm{raj}(w)$ is the degree of $\mathfrak{G}_w$, and $\bm{x}^{\operatorname{rajcode}(w)}$ is the leading monomial of its highest-degree homogeneous component. **Hafner's conjecture.** For $\ell(w)<k\leq \mathrm{raj}(w)$, 
$$
m_k(\bm{x})=x_p m_{k-1}(\bm{x}),
$$
 where $p$ is the largest index such that $x_p m_{k-1}(\bm{x})$ divides $\bm{x}^{\operatorname{rajcode}(w)}$. This conjecture gives a recursive description of the leading monomials of all positive-degree homogeneous components of a Grothendieck polynomial; its status is not specified in the source.

record.title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs
record.statement: Let $d>1$ be an integer. Let $q \equiv 1 \pmod {2d}$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $r$ be the largest integer such that $d \mid \frac{q-1}{p^r-1}$. The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ is a clique in the generalized Paley graph $GP(q,d)=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_q^+;(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^d)$. **Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture.** The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ forms a maximal clique in $GP(q,d)$. This conjecture asserts that the largest subfield producing a subfield clique cannot be extended to a larger clique. The paper resolves it in a stronger form under a sufficient-size hypothesis, while the unrestricted statement is the conjecture being addressed.
record.source_name: Chi Hoi Yip, “Maximality of subfields as cliques in Cayley graphs over finite fields”, arXiv:2209.00864 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2106.01522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.01522).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00864

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2022). “In , Yip described a similar phenomenon in Peisert graphs and conjectured that $\F_q$ forms a maximal clique in a Peisert graph with order $q^4$ provided that $q>3$; this was confirmed by Asgarli and Yip in .”

record.title: Conjecture on convex functions and Busemann functions
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a symmetric space of noncompact type. A function $f:M\to\mathbb{R}$ is **convex** if it is convex in the sense used for functions on $M$, and a **Busemann function** is a function $\beta:M\to\mathbb{R}$ associated with a geodesic ray in $M$. **Convex-function/Busemann-function conjecture.** For every convex function $f$ on $M$, there is a Busemann function $\beta:M\to\mathbb{R}$ and constants $a>0$ and $C\in\mathbb{R}$ such that, for every $x\in M$,

$$
f(x)>a\beta(x)+C.
$$

The conjecture seeks a universal Busemann lower bound for convex functions on symmetric spaces; the source presents it as further research after proving such a bound for functions arising from representation-theoretic data. The supplied status evidence says that an analogous conjecture for trees is false, but does not disprove this stated conjecture.
record.source_name: Omri N. Solan and Nattalie Tamam, “Geometric interpretation of quantitative instability”, arXiv:2209.01475 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01475

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2022). “The anlagous conjecture for trees is false: Let $G$ be a leafless $d$-regular tree, $x_0\in G$ a vertex and $(x_i)_{i=0}^\infty$ an infinite ray.”

record.title: 2-torsion and 4-torsion conjecture for double coverings of arrangement complements
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a complex hyperplane arrangement, let $M(\mathcal{A})$ be its complement, and let $\omega\in H^1(M(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{Z}_2)$. Denote by $M(\mathcal{A})^\omega$ the associated double covering and by $\mathcal{L}_\omega$ the rank-one local system determined by $\omega$. **2-torsion and 4-torsion conjecture.** The integral homology $H_1(M(\mathcal{A})^\omega,\mathbb{Z})$ has nontrivial $2$-torsion if and only if the local-system homology $H_1(M(\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{L}_\omega)$ has a $4$-torsion summand $\mathbb{Z}_4$. Examples in the source exhibit this relationship for specific arrangements, but the general equivalence is presented as a conjecture and its resolution is not given.

record.title: Liu's minimal mld conjecture for standard-coefficient Calabi-Yau pairs
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $(X,D)$ be the explicitly constructed klt Calabi-Yau pair in dimension $n$ with standard coefficients, namely the pair defined by the source's displayed construction. Its minimal log discrepancy is

$$
\frac{1}{s_{n+1}-1}.
$$

**Liu's minimal mld conjecture.** The number $1/(s_{n+1}-1)$ is the smallest possible minimal log discrepancy among all $n$-dimensional klt Calabi-Yau pairs with standard coefficients.

The claim proposes that Liu's example is extremal for minimal log discrepancies in this class. The source gives no resolution status.

record.title: The extremal orbifold Betti-number and Euler-characteristic conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and consider projective $n$-dimensional varieties with quotient singularities and trivial canonical class. Write $H$ for the sum of their orbifold Betti numbers. For odd $n$, write $\chi_{\mathrm{orb}}$ for the orbifold Euler characteristic. **Extremal orbifold invariants conjecture.** In dimension $n$, the largest possible value of $H$ is

$$
H=2(s_0-1)\cdots(s_n-1).
$$

For odd $n$, the smallest possible orbifold Euler characteristic is

$$
-(s_0-1)\cdots(s_{n-1}-1)(2s_n-6),
$$

and the largest is

$$
(s_0-1)\cdots(s_{n-1}-1)(2s_n-6).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by three explicit examples whose common Betti-number sum is the largest known for Calabi-Yau threefolds. The source gives no resolution status.

record.title: Conjecture on zeroes of functions in the evaluation space
record.statement:
Let $V$ be the function space under consideration, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be the evaluation set. Let $l$, $q$, $k$, and $i$ be the parameters used in the construction, and let the code's lower bound for the distance be the one given in Theorem.

**Zero-count conjecture.** Any function $f\in V$ will have fewer than

$$
lq^{k}+(k-1)(q-1)q^{k-1}+(q-2)q^{k-1}
$$

zeroes in $\mathcal{B}$, and therefore the lower bound for the distance in Theorem will not be attained for $i\geq 3$.

This conjecture predicts that the previously obtained distance lower bound is not sharp in the stated range, by ruling out functions attaining the corresponding maximum number of zeroes on the evaluation set. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Exact count conjecture for time-invariant Nash equilibria
record.statement:
Let $Q:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{N}$ denote the maximum cardinality of a set of mutually shift-inequivalent time-invariant Nash equilibria for the game $\operatorname{Standard}(x)$, and let $\lambda$ be the endpoint parameter for the admissible Mina-margin interval. **Exact-count conjecture.**

$$
Q(x)=2\quad\text{when }x\in(\lambda,\lambda^{-1}),\qquad Q(x)=1\quad\text{when }x\in\{\lambda,\lambda^{-1}\}.
$$

This refines the preceding existence result by asserting uniqueness up to shift in the interior and at both endpoints; the supplied text gives no resolution.

record.title: Conjecture on the normalized depth function of squarefree powers
record.statement:
Let $I$ be a squarefree monomial ideal in a polynomial ring $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. For each $k$ for which $I^{[k]}\neq 0$, let $d_k$ be the minimum degree of a monomial in the minimal generating set $G(I^{[k]})$, and define the **normalized depth function** by

$$
g_I(k)=\operatorname{depth}(S/I^{[k]})-(d_k-1).
$$

**Normalized-depth conjecture.** The function $g_I(k)$ is nonincreasing.

The paper presents this as a conjecture motivated by computations and examples, concerning the behavior of depths of squarefree powers; the supplied material gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open here.

record.title: Morse-Novikov genus conjecture for oriented links
record.statement:
For an oriented link $L$ in $S^3$, let $g_{{\rm{MN}}}(L)$ denote the minimum genus among possibly disconnected Seifert surfaces for $L$ that realize the Morse-Novikov number, and let $g(L)$ be the genus of $L$.

**Morse-Novikov genus conjecture.** One expects

$$
g_{{\rm{MN}}}(L)=g(L).
$$

This asserts that the Morse-Novikov genus is realized by a minimal-genus Seifert surface. The statement is not known in general, although the paper notes that for knots, and also for oriented links allowing disconnected Seifert surfaces, the Morse-Novikov genus is realized by an incompressible Seifert surface.

record.title: Endoscopic character identity for covers of reductive groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a reductive group with cover $G(F)_{x_G}$, let $(\dot s,\mathcal H)$ be a refined endoscopic datum for $G$, and let $H(F)_{x_H}$ be the corresponding endoscopic cover. Let $\varphi^G$ and $\varphi_H$ be tempered $L$-parameters related by the $L$-embedding $^L\xi_{H,G}$, and let $\Theta^{s,\mathsf{w}}_{\varphi_G}$ and $S\Theta_{\varphi_H}$ be the associated weighted and stable character distributions. If $f \in \mathcal C_c^\infty(G(F)_{x_G})$ and $f^H \in \mathcal C_c^\infty(H(F)_{x_H})$ are matching anti-genuine functions, then

$$
\Theta^{s,\mathsf{w}}_{\varphi_G}(f)=S\Theta_{\varphi_H}(f^H).
$$

Equivalently, for strongly regular semi-simple elements and the transfer factor $\Delta'_x[\mathsf{w}]$,

$$
\Theta^{s,\mathsf{w}}_{\varphi_G}(\delta_G)=\sum_\gamma \Delta'_x[\mathsf{w}](\gamma_H,\delta_G)S\Theta_{\varphi_H}(\gamma_H),
$$

where the sum runs over strongly regular semi-simple elements $\gamma$ of $H(F)$ up to stable conjugacy, and $\gamma_H\in H(F)_{x_H}$ is an arbitrary lift of $\gamma$. This is the expected character identity for refined endoscopic transfer in the setting of covers of reductive groups; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for Markov fractions
record.statement: Let $q$ be a Markov number, and call a rational number a Markov fraction when it is one of the Markov fractions defined in the paper; its denominator is the denominator in lowest terms. The interval under consideration is $[0,\frac{1}{2}]$. **Uniqueness conjecture for Markov fractions.** For each Markov number $q$, the interval $[0,\frac{1}{2}]$ contains at most one Markov fraction with denominator $q$. This is equivalent to the uniqueness conjecture for Markov numbers, which asserts that every Markov number is the maximum of exactly one ordered Markov triple; the proposition is stated as yet to be proved or refuted.
